title: City Day places
description: One city's config and every place City Day can reveal there. A place is never added from a guess: each one has a source and the hours it was checked against. Two keywords go beyond standard JSON Schema: calendarDate (a real day, so not 2026-02-31) and startBeforeEnd (the first hour is before the second). A validator that doesn't know them skips them, so the page checks the same two things itself when it loads the file.

$schema.description: Points an editor at this schema.

city.description: The city's full name. The page shows it on the day's first screen and on the creator's desk, and it is how an old saved day that says the name finds its city.

cityId.description: Lowercase, starting with a letter. Never change: sent links carry it. Unique across every city file.

short.description: The short name for lines like 'A day in St. Pete'.

region.description: Added after a typed place in Get directions when the typed place doesn't already name the region, such as FL.

regionNames.description: Lowercase ways a typed place can already name the region, such as fl and florida.

timeZone.description: An IANA time zone name, such as America/New_York. The page runs the day's clock in it.

weather.description: Where the forecast is read from. Must be inside National Weather Service coverage, to 3 decimals.

sun.description: Where sunrise and sunset are worked out. Kept apart from weather because the two don't share a precision.

rainLine.description: One line on local rain, shown on the plan B screen after the forecast. Leave it out when there is nothing true to say.

fixture.description: True for a test-only city. The page never offers it.

stops.description: The places, in the order the page keeps them. Order breaks ties, so moving one can change a day.

id.description: Never rename or delete: sent links refer to it.

name.description: The place's name as shown on screen.

address.description: Street address shown under the name.

query.description: What the Get directions button searches for in maps. The page builds the link from this.

hint.description: One practical line about the visit, from the place's own page.

tags.description: Words a note can match, such as coffee or museum. A museum tag is what 'no museums' removes.

costBand.description: Price level of a meal or a dinner. null means not recorded.

cost.description: ticket is paid entry. small is a small fee. null means not recorded or free.

week.description: The window City Day offers each weekday, 0 is Sunday. [open, close] in 24-hour time, null when closed. A close past midnight is written as 25, 27 and so on. It is not always the source's label: see hoursLabel and hoursText.

closedDates.description: Dates the place says it is closed. Use [] when there are none.

source.description: The page the hours and facts came from.

hoursChecked.description: The day the hours were last checked against the source. null means no check date was ever recorded.

why.description: The line about the place. The page adds 'Its own site lists <hours> <day>.' after it. Use this or whyText, not both.

whyText.description: The whole line about the place, with no sentence added after it. May use {hours}, {on}, {occ} and {when}: the hours shown, 'today' or 'on Saturday', 'a date', and the date. Use this or why, not both.

whyByDate.description: A line that replaces whyText on one date, for a one-day event at a place that is otherwise regular.

feel.description: Which 'What's calling?' pool the place can come up in. Leave it out for a dinner or parking only.

meal.description: What kind of food stop this is. Leave it out for places that are not a meal.

menuFocus.description: What the kitchen centers on, from its own menu. Only a seafood-centric place is kept off for 'no seafood'.

menuSource.description: The menu page menuFocus came from.

menuChecked.description: The day the menu was last read.

dinner.description: True when the place can be the evening dinner.

parking.description: True for the parking garage, which is offered only when the note mentions driving.

booking.description: True when a reservation is needed, so it only comes up when the note asks for that kind of thing.

outdoor.description: True when the place is outside, so it is left out on a rainy day.

music.description: True when music is part of the place.

kids.description: True when the place suits kids.

gem.description: True for a lesser-known place. Left out means true.

bar.description: True when the place is a bar or brewery. It is only offered to someone who said yes to drinks.

dated.description: True for a one-day or one-weekend event. It leads the day when it is on.

only.description: Short words for when a dated place happens, such as 'this weekend only'.

covers.description: The id of a place this event stands in for, so the day does not show both.

order.description: Tie-break, lowest first. Left out means 20.

split.description: A break in the day, by weekday: [start, end] hours when the place is closed between its lunch and dinner service.

opensBeforeSunrise.description: Hours before sunrise the place opens. The opening time is worked out for the date and replaces week's open time.

closesAfterSunset.description: Hours after sunset the place closes. The closing time is worked out for the date and replaces week's close time.

lastEntry.description: The place's own last entry or admission time: one hour, or one per weekday.

lastEntryText.description: The source's exact sentence about last entry, when hoursText does not hold it.

hoursText.description: The source's own hours, copied word for word. Not shown on screen.

hoursLabel.description: The hours text shown for the place, as one string or one per weekday. Left out, the text is built from week.

lister.description: Who says the hours, in place of 'Its own site lists'.

skipDates.description: Dates the source lists shorter hours or an event this file cannot hold. The place is not offered then.

openDates.description: The only dates the place is open. For a one-day event.

months.description: The months the place is open, 1 to 12. For a seasonal place.

label.description: The hours text shown on that date.

start.description: The hour the place opens on that date.

end.description: The hour the place closes on that date.

dateHours.description: Hours that replace the weekday's on one date, such as a holiday with short hours.
